text:
jamie: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — wanted to distill the leadership answers into a short internal cheat sheet. tossing a few questions here.

rebecca: thanks jamie. first ask: what's the one-sentence distinction vs hyperscalers that we want everyone to use?

carlos: i'd say: 'Redwood focuses on predictable inference economics and operational control across hosted-to-private deployments, instead of bundling compute and model licensing into one opaque stack.'

nina: shorter variant for sales: 'Predictable latency, measurable unit cost, and a straight path to private deployments.'

alex: for technical audiences we should also have a 10-15s follow-up: 'GPU-optimized runtime with continuous batching, KV cache, smart routing, and quant-friendly paths — so you get consistent tail latency and lower per-token cost.' keep it optional.

sam: are we okay with public collateral naming hyperscalers? customers ask directly.

rebecca: public collateral -> categories only. in RFPs or customer calls, be specific and back claims with bench links. ops-bot: please pin the canonical bench URL.

ops-bot: canonical bench: https://redwood.internal/bench/2025-q4 (internal access only)

jamie: next: RFP playbook — who owns competitive notes and the cost comparison table?

carlos: product + solutions should own the baseline table, sales can annotate with customer-specific numbers. i'll add a template to the shared drive.

nina: small comms item: can we get a short FAQ entry for 'When to choose Dedicated vs Private' — i can draft copy for the docs site.

alex: will add an engineering note about migration complexity. include a tiny snippet engineers can paste into proposals:

```
Hosted -> Dedicated: reserve capacity and predictable throughput (no code change).
Dedicated -> Private: network/KMS integration, minor config changes, same API surface.
```

rebecca: love that. final thing: privacy/compliance questions — who signs off on the standard answer? legal or product?

jamie: legal for anything contractual, product for technical guarantees. rebecca, i'll arrange a quick sync with legal to lock the approved wording.

rebecca: done — i'll schedule a 30-min sync and circulate a canonical paragraph after. thanks team.
